Campus drives

Companies

These cards describe the usual public pattern for each company. The exact test changes by year and college. Use Ask AI when you want a plan for one of them.

TCS

IT services

Tata Consultancy Services hires a large share of Indian campuses, often through the National Qualifier Test and a later interview.

  1. 1. Online test

    Usually numerical ability, verbal ability, reasoning, and a programming section. The mix depends on the NQT variant.

  2. 2. Technical interview

    Projects, one programming language, DBMS or OOP basics, and sometimes a short coding or SQL question.

  3. 3. HR interview

    Relocation, gaps, and why TCS. Offer bands such as Ninja, Digital, and Prime have been used, but names and cutoffs change.

  • Practice timed aptitude before long coding sessions.
  • Be ready to explain your final-year project without slides.

Infosys

IT services

Infosys campus drives usually combine an online assessment with a technical round and an HR conversation.

  1. 1. Online assessment

    Aptitude, verbal, logical reasoning, and often a coding or hands-on section. Some years use InfyTQ-style practice before the drive.

  2. 2. Technical interview

    Programming fundamentals, a project deep dive, and basic questions from DBMS, OS, or the student's elective.

  3. 3. HR interview

    Communication, flexibility on location, and a clear introduction.

  • Write a 90-second self introduction and practice it aloud.
  • Revise one language deeply rather than five shallowly.

Wipro

IT services

Wipro campus hiring often starts with an online assessment and continues with technical and HR rounds.

  1. 1. Online assessment

    English, quantitative aptitude, and logical reasoning. Some drives add an essay or a coding question.

  2. 2. Technical interview

    Language basics, project work, and simple problem solving.

  3. 3. HR interview

    Goals, strengths, and willingness to work in shifts or relocate.

  • Do not ignore the English section.
  • Keep one academic project and one personal project ready.

Accenture

IT services and consulting

Accenture campus assessments often test cognitive skills, technical basics, and communication before an interview.

  1. 1. Cognitive and technical assessment

    Reasoning, English, and role-related technical questions. Coding appears for some developer tracks.

  2. 2. Communication check

    A short speaking or listening task is common. Clear speech matters as much as the score.

  3. 3. Interview

    Projects, fundamentals, and fit. The interviewer may mix technical and HR questions in one sitting.

  • Practice explaining a project in simple English.
  • Revise pseudocode and basic complexity, not only syntax.

Cognizant

IT services

Cognizant GenC-style drives usually stack an online test, a technical discussion, and HR. The cluster of tests changes by hiring season.

  1. 1. Online assessment

    Quantitative, logical, and verbal questions, sometimes with a coding or debugging cluster.

  2. 2. Technical interview

    Programming, SQL or DBMS, and whatever you listed on the resume.

  3. 3. HR interview

    Background, relocation, and why Cognizant.

  • Only list skills you can speak about for five minutes.
  • Practice debugging small programs on paper.

Capgemini

IT services

Capgemini campus processes often include an aptitude or game-style assessment, a technical round, and HR.

  1. 1. Online assessment

    Quantitative and logical questions. Some drives use game-based tasks or pseudocode instead of a long coding paper.

  2. 2. Technical interview

    Language of your choice, one project, and a few fundamentals.

  3. 3. HR interview

    Communication and willingness to learn a new stack after joining.

  • Read pseudocode questions slowly.
  • Prepare an answer for a tool you want to learn on the job.

Amazon

Product

Amazon intern and new-grad loops focus on coding and Leadership Principles. This is a different pattern from a service-company aptitude test.

  1. 1. Online assessment

    Coding problems and sometimes a work-style survey. Debugging or work-simulation tasks appear in some seasons.

  2. 2. Technical interviews

    Data structures, algorithms, and complexity. You are expected to talk through the approach before coding.

  3. 3. Behavioral interviews

    Stories mapped to Leadership Principles, with a specific situation, what you did, and the result.

  • Practice medium DSA problems out loud.
  • Prepare four STAR stories that are actually yours.

Microsoft

Product

Microsoft campus hiring for technical roles is centered on coding interviews and project depth, after an online assessment.

  1. 1. Online assessment

    Coding problems, sometimes with a short debugging or multiple-choice technical section.

  2. 2. Technical interviews

    DSA, problem solving, and follow-ups on your approach. Interviewers often ask why a solution is correct.

  3. 3. Final discussion

    More problem solving or a conversation about internships and projects. An HR screen may be separate.

  • Write clean code and test it with one example.
  • Be ready to improve a brute-force answer.

HCLTech

IT services

HCLTech campus drives commonly use an aptitude test followed by technical and HR rounds.

  1. 1. Aptitude test

    Quantitative aptitude, logical reasoning, and verbal ability under a time limit.

  2. 2. Technical interview

    C, Java, or Python basics, plus DBMS and your project.

  3. 3. HR interview

    Introduction, family background questions are less useful than clarity about role and location.

  • Time-box aptitude sets to 30 minutes.
  • Revise DBMS keys, normalization, and one join query.
